correctness.rationale: The open-neighborhood proof characterizes exactly all minimum triples, including all m,n≥3 boundaries. One product-edge slide simultaneously changes row and column, giving regular degree 3(m-3)(n-3). At 4x4 the unique perfect-matching completion is invariant and each fiber is K4. The three listed finite slide templates are checked for every intermediate partial matching and realize generating row/column swaps whenever a spare row and two spare columns exist; transposition covers the dual case. Jump connectivity follows from independently adjustable one-coordinate endpoints with a spare slot. Both independent-style checkers execute directly from the packaged source and reproduce counts/structures in their documented finite domains. Finite data do not substitute for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Henning–Kazemi (2011 online) gives the scalar minimum 3 but not the exact set classifications, one-slide components, 24 four-cliques, or connectivity templates. The 2017 total dominating reconfiguration study permits addition/removal and includes nonminimal supersets rather than the present minimum-exchange state space. Semantic mathematical-record matches concerned complete multipartite graphs, rook Cartesian products, partial matching complexes, and other problems, none implying a simultaneous-free-row/free-column slide classification on categorical products. Earlier related rook-graph claims use Cartesian rather than categorical products. Targeted primary searches found no stronger covering theorem; this is best-knowledge originality rather than proof of absolute priority.
residual_risks: A previous equivalent restricted-matching-exchange result may exist under unindexed terminology; literature searches cannot establish absolute priority.
Only the abstract of the 2020 survey was accessible; it was not used to assert full-document absence.

value.rationale: The sharp boundary between frozen 3-by-n products, 24 isolated four-clique sectors at 4-by-4, and connected minimum-set mobility starting 4-by-5 is a structural phase transition in minimum total domination, rather than a small scalar improvement. The square case has a natural conserved completion to a perfect matching; two spare columns permit explicit finite generating paths that break that invariant. Counting every optimum and transition for all factor sizes shows the exact scope. This is not an automatic restatement of the known scalar minimum.
